tossups.text: This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for bronchi and bronchioles. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this bronchus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The bronchus is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in bronchi and bronchioles.

tossups.text: This process limits the rate of catalytically perfect enzymes. A coefficient describing this process is equal to mobility times temperature times Boltzmann's constant according to the Einstein-Smoluchowski relation. According to Fick's first law, the flux of this process is proportional to the negative of the gradient of concentration. When water undergoes this process, it is called osmosis. For 10 points, identify this process in which particles move from areas of high concentration to low concentration.

James Bugental developed his humanistic approach to psychotherapy after reading the works of this psychologist. One of this man's works links intentionality with the "wish," a playful digression on the thoughts of the future. He also wrote The Springs of Creative Living, in which he labeled atheists as those that lack "authenticity." He distinguished between normal breakdowns and neurotic breakdowns in one work in his The Meaning of Anxiety. He included innocence, rebellion, ordinary, and creative as the four stages that are part of a development of a human being. He also used a term to describe the state in between "fallenness" and "throwness" in his works inspired by his good friend Paul Tillich. For 10 points, identify this existential psychologist whose works like Love and Will and The Courage to Create display his fondness for interpreting destiny.

Robert Bultmann argued that the semeia source was an incomplete version of this book that was authored by a person in it who is told, "Here is your mother." Some scholars believe that the week of creation is mirrored in this book in its section the "Book of Signs." Christ is referred to as "the bread of life," "the light of the world," and "the true vine" as part of seven "I am" statements in this book. The statement that one man "wept" in this book makes up the shortest verse in the Bible. In this book's second chapter, Jesus turns water into wine at a wedding in Cana. This book's equating of Jesus with God is illustrated by its opening sentence,"In the beginning was the Word." For 10 points, name this non-synoptic gospel, the final of the four gospels in the New Testament.

This musician listed himself under a fake name so that he could play with Dizzy Gillespie at Massey Hall and avoid a contract dispute. This musician's tunes "Ah-Leu-Cha" and "Anthropology" were contrafacts based on "I Got Rhythm," a song that this musician once performed so badly that Jo Jones threw a cymbal at him. The session where this musician first recorded his tune "Ko-Ko" is thought to be the first-ever bebop recording session. This musician adapted the standard "How High the Moon" into "Ornithology," a tune whose title was inspired by his nickname. For 10 points, name this alto saxophonist nicknamed "Bird."
acceptableAnswers: as that’s the fake name he played under

tossups.text: An author with this last name included poems like "The Swan" and "The Albatross" in his collection The Flowers of Evil. A fictional couple with this last name were members of the VFD and were the parents of a girl who ties her hair back in a ribbon to think. Count Olaf is the main enemy of three children with this last name. For 10 points, give this last name of Violet, Klaus, and Sunny in Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events.

A motif named for this element is combined with the cleavage domain of FokI in a useful genome-editing enzyme. Insulin molecules surround an ion of this element in hexameric form. Two histidine residues and two cysteine residues coordinate an ion of this element in a common protein structural motif. This metal is found in the active site of the majority of carbonic anhydrases. This element inhibits the binding of rhinovirus receptors in a common pharmaceutical usage. This metal is found in a common DNA binding motif called a "finger." For 10 points, name this element that is found in cold-relieving supplements and has symbol Zn.

A zinc selenide crystal causes total internal reflection in the attenuated total reflectance type of this technique. The two dimensional form of this technique is used to dynamically follow hydrogen bond formation. Unlike a similar technique, this technique requires a compound to have a change in its dipole moment rather than a permanent dipole. This technique can detect certain motions like rocking, wagging, and scissoring. Samples are prepared for this process using Nujol oil or a potassium bromide pellet. Carbonyl compounds have a peak of about 1700 wavenumbers, and several useful vibrations occur in the "fingerprint" region of its spectrum. For 10 points, name this type of spectroscopy that causes vibrations using wavelengths longer than visible light.

This man wrote an essay in which he questioned why dogs don't form rational ideas, entitled "Brute and Human Intellect," and in a later work, he called for a scientific determination of the limits of human ability in "The Energies of Man." He proposed that a genuine option must be live, momentous, and forced in a volume that included the essays, "Reflex Action and Theism," "Is Life Worth Living?," and the title essay, "The Will to Believe." This man also claimed that one must not consider an object's physical derivation when making a value judgement. For 10 points, name this author of The Varieties of Religious Experience, Principles of Psychology and a work titled after this man's school, Pragmatism.

This compound and hydrochloric acid are reacted with aromatic hydrocarbons in the Gattermann-Koch reaction. The two main components of syngas are hydrogen and this compound, which also reacts with chlorine to produce phosgene. This compound reacts with water in the water gas shift reaction, and this compound reacts with nickel in the Mond process. The effect of hydrogen ions and this compound on the binding ability of hemoglobin for oxygen is known as the Bohr effect. In a catalytic converter, platinum metal catalyzes the conversion of this toxic compound into a non-toxic compound. For 10 points, name this gas present in automobile exhaust that has formula CO.

It mentions people who "in humorless protest overturned only one symbolic pingpong table." Other figures in this work include the "Chinaman of Oklahoma," people who "journeyed to Denver," "died in Denver," and "came back to Denver and waited in vain," and others who "ate fire in paint hotels or drank turpentine in Paradise Alley." Another passage refers to people who "sat through the stale beer afternoon in desolate Fugazzi's, listening to the crack of doom on the hydrogen jukebox." This work is dedicated to a man who met its author while both were at the Columbia Psychiatric Institute, Carl Solomon. For 10 points, name this poem that begins "I saw the best minds of my generation destroyed by madness," a work by Allen Ginsberg.

Monuments at this place include a small tower called the Torreón and a carved stone whose precise placement in alignment with the sun at the two equinoxes suggests its use as an astronomical observatory. Entry into this place was only possible through roads near Salcantay and the Lucumayo valley, and, while quipus were used here as means of keeping records, they remain untranslatable. It is believed that it served as a retreat for Pachacuti Yupanqui, who had conquered the region of Tampu. The Spanish arrived at this place in 1532, burning many shrines and trails to it until it was rediscovered by Hiram Bingham in 1911. For 10 points, name this Peruvian site around 50 miles northwest of Cuzco, formerly built by the Inca.

A story by this author ends with the declaration that "my solitude is cheered by that elegant hope" and features an epigraph from The Anatomy of Melancholy. In another work by this author, a letter reading "the first letter of the name has been uttered" is left on a rabbi's typewriter, and Red Scharlach uses the pattern of the Tetragrammaton to lure and kill Erik Lonnrot. This author created Carlos Danieri, who finds a spot in his cellar that shows every point in the universe. "Purifiers" destroy books deemed nonsense in infinite hexagonal rooms created by this author of "The Aleph" and "The Library of Babel." For 10 points, name this Argentinian short story writer of Ficciones.

An old textbook in this novel has a picture of Venus de Milo with a crudely-drawn moustache and armpit hair. A character in this novel is only able to say "I didn't..." before a woman kicks his head three times to end his misery during a "particicution." That character is revealed to be part of the Mayday Resistance against the Gilead regime established by the Commander in this novel. Offred is one of the title women who are forced to bear children in, for 10 points, what dystopian novel by Margaret Atwood?

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for axial skeleton bones. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this skull-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The skull is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in axial skeleton bones.

tossups.text: In human anatomy, this structure is essential for complement system. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this phagocyte-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The phagocyte is a key component of the Immune system, involved in complement system.

tossups.text: The muddy upper portion of this river is joined with a smaller blackwater river at the Meeting of Waters. The Marañón ("mah-rah-nee-AWN") was the main candidate in a 20th-century dispute over the source of this river, which has no bridge crossings or dams. This river contains the largest population of a species of pink river dolphin known as the boto. This river provides access to the largest city unreachable by road, Iquitos. The capital of a state named for this river is Manaus ("mah-NOWSE"). A disputed claim ranks this river, rather than one in Africa, as the longest river in the world due to its source in the Peruvian Andes. For 10 points, name this South American river that runs through a vast rainforest.

One technique named for this adjective was first performed using gadolinium phosphomolybdate tridecahydrate by William Giauque ("jee-OAK"). In that process named for this adjective, a paramagnetic salt in equilibrium with a liquid helium bath is first magnetized, then the helium is removed and the temperature drops to values as low as 1 millikelvin due to this type of "demagnetization." A steeply-sloped hyperbola on a PV diagram represents this type of process, for which the product of pressure times volume raised to the power of the heat capacity ratio is constant. A process that is reversible and has this property is isentropic. For 10 points, the Carnot cycle pairs two isothermal processes with what type of process that has no heat transfer?

The First Council of this religion was called because one of its adherents had argued that followers could act as they wished after the death of this religion's greatest leader. That council set the rules for this religion's monastic community, the sangha. This religion's doctrine of the two truths, referring to the distinction between conventional and ultimate reality, was promulgated by Nagarjuna. A central tenet of this religion is the desire to eliminate dukkha, or the suffering created by craving. For 10 points, what religion includes central texts like the Lotus and Heart Sutras, and was created by Siddhartha Gautama.

An investigation into this event criticized the "laxity" of the British Board of Trade and was led by Senator William Alden Smith. Molly Brown created a Survivors' Committee after this event, and this incident was partially caused after radio warnings from the Mesaba and the Californian were ignored. J. Bruce Ismay, the chairman of White Star Line, was criticized for escaping in a lifeboat during this event, which took the lives of Benjamin Guggenheim and John Jacob Astor. For 10 points, name this 1912 disaster in which a supposedly "unsinkable" passenger liner collided with an iceberg.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with sebaceous glands.
What is the main function of the hair follicle in the integumentary system?
Name another component of the integumentary system related to sebaceous glands.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human integumentary system.

parts.text: This is the minimum amount of energy that an isolated, gaseous atom in the ground state must absorb to discharge an electron. This quantity generally increases from left to right across each period, peaking at the noble gases.
This value, a measure of the size of an atom, is usually measured in picometers. It usually decreases to the right and increases downwards.
Atomic radius is substantially affected by this effect, in which the inner shell electrons lower the effective nuclear charge enacted on valence electrons.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about trends found in the periodic table. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this decision-theoretic puzzle concerning an individual who is put to sleep for two days and then is awakened one or twice depending on the flip of a coin.

Since Beauty cannot learn the probability that she was awakened once by conditionalizing on her priors, many view the problem as an objection to this man's namesake non-frequentist interpretation of probability.

Ian Hacking used Bayesian decision theory to analyze this argument from the Pensées ("pon-SAY"). It contends that you should live as though God exists since you are only risking a finite amount of utility for a potentially infinite amount.

bonuses.leadin: Adam Elga introduced this puzzle in a short 2000 paper that uses self-locating beliefs to argue for its "thirder" answer. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this book about "feminism and the subversion of identity" by Judith Butler, which argues that its title concept is performative.
acceptableAnswers: Gender Trouble: Feminism and the Subversion of Identity

parts.text: In Gender Trouble, Butler compares this philosopher's asymmetric gender theory to that of Luce Irigaray. This French philosopher stated that "one is not born a woman, but rather becomes one" in her book The Second Sex.
acceptableAnswers: Simone Lucie Ernestine Marie Bertrand de Beauvoir

parts.text: Gender Trouble claims that an earlier thinker's writings on Herculine Barbin's journal contradict his arguments given in this book. This book's first volume, "The Will to Knowledge," criticizes the "regressive hypothesis."

bonuses.leadin: This book introduced the term "heterosexual matrix" to refer to the societal norm of presumed heterosexuality, naturally othering sexual minorities. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this instrument, which is imitated by the brass in the first movement of Ernest Bloch's Schelomo for cello and orchestra.

A moment reminiscent of a shofar blast has been theorized as one of several Jewish influences on this C minor symphony. This symphony sets a text from Des Knaben Wunderhorn ("dess K'NAH-ben VOON-der-horn") in its fourth movement "Urlicht" ("OOR-leekt") for solo alto.

Jewish-inspired themes in classical music are more commonly played by this instrument, such as in Prokofiev's Overture on Hebrew Themes. This single-reed woodwind often plays the melody in klezmer bands.

bonuses.leadin: This instrument is played offstage just before some Watchers sing "It shines!" during a scene from Edward Elgar's The Apostles, although it is often replaced with a flugelhorn in performance. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this officer from Pianosa whose disastrous investment in Egyptian cotton forced him to try to sell it in his mess hall in the form of cotton candy.
Milo was regarded by everyone as a jerk except this man, who regarded him as a genius as well. He followed his roommate Orr's original plan and fled to Sweden.

Yossarian kept trying to have this man ground him so he won't have to fly more missions; however, he is unsympathetic and keeps talking about his former clinic on Staten Island that had a corner location.

bonuses.leadin: He inserted the ampersand in his namesake company to dispel any idea that it is a one-man operation. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this technique in which cycles of annealing and elongation are used to amplify a piece of DNA.
These undesirable by-products in PCR form due to improper hybridization. Hot start PCR may reduce the formation of these things.
Primer dimer formation is made more likely by high levels of these two nucleobases, which increase DNA annealing temperatures due to forming three hydrogen bonds.

bonuses.leadin: Fluorescent probes like taqman (rhymes with "pacman") can be used in a quantitative form of this technique for measuring gene expression. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these phenomena that occur along Wadati-Benioff zones.
This variety of earthquake occurs when the speed of the rupture exceeds that of the S-wave velocity.
Earthquakes can be induced by human activity, including this method of breaking up underground rocks.

bonuses.leadin: When these events occur, they can lead to soil liquefaction. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this esoteric religious group that incorporates elements from Islam, gnosticism, neoplatonism, Christianity, Buddhism, and Hinduism. They use the Khams Hudud as a religious symbol.
The Druze venerate this man whom they call Shu'ayb ("shoe-ibe"). He was the father-in-law of Moses in the Old Testament.

The Druze faith was founded after several followers of Fatimid Caliph al-Hakim claimed him to be this figure. Twelver Shi'a Muslims believe the 12th Imam to be this figure, who along with Isa will come again at the end of the world.

bonuses.leadin: Despite not considering themselves Muslims, this group is considered as Muslims for Lebanese parliament apportionment. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Identify this quantity which is equal to the second central moment of a distribution.
Homoscedasticity is an important assumption for this regression technique which involves finding the best fit line by minimizing the second power of the residuals.
Ordinary least squares was developed by this German mathematician, whose namesake law implies that the electric flux through a surface is proportional to the charge enclosed by the surface.

bonuses.leadin: Homoscedasticity describes conditions in which this quantity remains the same across various groups of data. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Sidi marries Baroka in The Lion and the Jewel, a play by Wole Soyinka, an author from this country.
Naguib Mahfouz hails from this capital city. He included Palace Walk, Palace of Desire, and Sugar Street in his trilogy depicting life in this city.

This country is home to Nuruddin Farah, whose novel From a Crooked Rib details the life of Ebla. Farah has spoken out against the widespread violence in this country, which was home to the Islamic Courts Union.

bonuses.leadin: Name some African locales based on their literary output, for 10 points each.

parts.text: In 1846, the National Anti-Slavery Standard singled out this clause as the Constitution's worst. This infamous "compromise" ignored Native Americans and counted the enslaved as fractional people to apportion representatives.

The Fugitive Slave Act led northern states to pass personal liberty laws to protect this right. After riots in Baltimore, Justice Taney ruled that President Lincoln could not suspend this right in Ex parte Merryman.

After he escaped slavery to Ontario, Henry Bibb argued that South Carolina violated this clause by imprisoning free Black sailors. This clause in Article Four prohibits interstate discrimination and affords the right to travel.

bonuses.leadin: Michael F. Conlin argued that antebellum sectional debates often drew on legal arguments in The Constitutional Origins of the American Civil War. For 10 points each:

parts.text: In this language you will hear some words like Duckspeak, bellyfeel, crimethink, and unperson. It is from the book 1984.
Words in this Russian based-language are Platties, chelloveck, britva, droog. Alex uses it in A Clockwork Orange.
Hrududu, marli, ni-frith, and hrair are words in this language, spoken by bunnies in Watership Down.

parts.text: Name these creatures. In the Odyssey, Penelope knows that her husband will soon return home after a prophetic dream in which an eagle descending from a mountain slaughters twenty of these birds.

One of the first classical poems learned by children of this country starts with the line, "Goose, goose, goose" and describes "white feathers on the emerald water." That poem is by Luò Bīnwáng, a Tang poet of this country.

Mary Oliver's poem "Wild Geese" opens by telling the reader that "You do not have to be [this concept]." Gwendolyn Brooks' "The Bean Eaters" describes the title pair as "Two who are Mostly [this concept]."
acceptableAnswers: “You do not have to be good”

What is the main function of the spinal cord in the nervous system?

What is the main function of the diaphragm in the respiratory system?

parts.text: Name this member of the Channel Islands that is actually located 22 miles from the mainland.
Catalina is located off the coast of this state, whose national parks include Yosemite.
Catalina is also home to a Memorial and Botanic Garden named for this chewing gum magnate, who owned a share of the Chicago Cubs during the 1920s.

parts.text: Name this high-energy light-matter interaction that occurs near atomic nuclei. On a Feynman ("FINE-min") diagram, it is represented by a squiggly arrow splitting into two straight arrows.
That form of pair production produces one of these negatively-charged fermions along with its antiparticle, the positron.
Pair production is the reverse reaction of this other process, in which an electron and a positron collide. At low energies, this process creates at least 2 photons.

bonuses.leadin: In order for a photon to undergo this process, it must have an energy of at least 1.022 mega-electron-volts. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this concept, the title subject of a discourse by Jean-Jacques Rousseau that calls the first man to have enclosed a piece of land and declared "this is mine!" the founder of civil society.

Rousseau's Discourse on Inequality was wrongly accused of promoting the "noble savage" due to its discussion of this condition that humans existed in before society formed. Hobbes called life in this state "a war of all against all" and "nasty, brutish, and short."
Discourse on Inequality contrasts a form of this concept that causes primitive man to preserve his own well-being with a more harmful type in which people are aware of how others perceive them.

bonuses.leadin: A discourse on this concept was followed by its author's Discourse on Political Economy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this state whose politics were once heavily influenced by Boss Tweed. A later member of Tammany Hall, Al Smith, governed it for 4 terms from Albany.
Tammany hall was named after the Lenape leader Tamanend, who was given this title shared with the leader of Tammany Hall.
This republican mayor of New York City notably defeated Tammany Hall. He remade many jobs to be based on merit rather than patronage now names an airport in Queens.

bonuses.leadin: The Locofoco faction of the Democratic party was founded in this state to oppose Tammany Hall. For 10 points each:
